paper_metadata.title: Exploring Quantum Neural Networks for Demand Forecasting

summary: The paper evaluates a hybrid variational quantum neural network for forecasting vehicle financing demand using a proprietary dataset of 52 monthly samples. Across feature sets (4, 8, and 19 features) and circuit depths (1–5 layers), the best quantum result achieves a 12‑month mean absolute error of about 682±284, while a classical RNN baseline can reach MAE ≈344 when excluding anomalous months. All experiments were performed as PennyLane simulations rather than on quantum hardware.

experiments.description: Quantum neural network for short-term demand forecasting of used vehicle financing in Brazil, evaluated on three feature sets (4, 8, and 19 features) and three variational depths (1, 3, and 5 layers), with two quantum experiment variants compared against a classical RNN baseline.

algorithm.variant: variational quantum neural network (hybrid QNN) with feature-map RY encoding and two entanglement patterns
algorithm.ansatz: layered parameterized quantum circuit with Hadamard feature preparation, RY data encoding, entanglement layer 1 or 2, and parametrized single-qubit rotations R(θ, ϕ, ω)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: training stopped at 30 epochs based on rapid convergence observed in preliminary 1000-epoch tests

problem_formulation.encoding_details: classical features encoded into qubits using Hadamard gates followed by RY(x_i) rotations; one qubit per feature in the depicted 4-qubit circuit, with analogous scaling for larger feature sets not explicitly detailed
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize mean absolute error for demand forecasting of used vehicle financing

problem_instance.description: Forecasting monthly demand for used vehicle financing in Brazil

dataset_specification.target: daily average of used vehicle financing each month
dataset_specification.feature_selection: 6 of 25 features removed because they lacked 2019 data; PCA used to create 4-feature and 8-feature subsets from 19 remaining features

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: removed 6 features without 2019 values; applied PCA to 19 remaining features to obtain 4-feature and 8-feature subsets; standardized features using z-score normalization; kept pandemic-period data; no imputation for missing 2019 values
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 independent runs per configuration; evaluated by monthly mean absolute error and standard deviation over the 12-month test period

implementation_details.classical_solver: TensorFlow training for the hybrid QNN; classical RNN baselines with 128 and 1024 neurons in the recurrent layer
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: mean absolute error and standard deviation computed from 10 runs
implementation_details.total_execution_time: Quantum simulations: 4-feature models 1.5-5 min per run; 8-feature models 3-10 min per run; 19-feature models 1-3.5 h per run

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: rapid convergence with marginal or zero improvement after ~30 epochs

speedup_claims.conditions: simulation on PennyLane/TensorFlow HPC environment; faster convergence and fewer parameters were observed
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not establish an asymptotic or hardware-demonstrated quantum speedup; it only reports faster convergence in simulation and comparable accuracy in the best cases.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: unknown; experiments simulated up to ~19 qubits with shallow variational circuits (1–5 layers)
limiting_factors: all experiments performed on classical simulators rather than quantum hardware
classical RNN baseline achieves lower error in best case (MAE ≈344 vs quantum ≈682 for comparable configuration)
no asymptotic complexity advantage claimed or demonstrated
quantum model performance comparable but not superior

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states all simulations were performed in PennyLane on an HPC environment and explicitly says the problem was solved through simulation, not on a quantum computer.

num_qubits inferred from the 4-feature circuit figure showing four qubits; the paper does not explicitly state qubit counts for the 8- and 19-feature cases, but the architecture is feature-to-qubit angle encoding.
speedup_order set to none_proven because the paper discusses faster convergence and shorter execution times in simulation but does not establish an asymptotic quantum speedup.
The paper claims similar predictive performance and faster convergence with fewer parameters, but does not claim a computational speedup or demonstrate superior accuracy.
Classical RNN achieves MAE ≈344 (excluding anomalous months) compared to quantum best mean ≈682, indicating classical still performs better.
